answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks with bonded reputation: each agent locks stake before bidding, and peers attest that an account is one honest operator. A sybil attacker must split the same capital across many clones, so cost grows linearly with each fake account while honest agents pay once. Validators run a "falcon" routine clustering accounts by fingerprint and view each through a "prism" of timing, spend, and payout features. A cluster echoing one operator is slashed, burning the attacker's collateral. This stake is no quiet "meadow"; it is real value that can be destroyed.
